comparator.name: Media and Culture
comparator.route: Dutch-language track — Performing Arts and Creative Technologies
comparator.sourceNotes: The Dutch-track example comprises a 120 EC major and 60 EC of profiling space. It illustrates Performing Arts and Creative Technologies, taught in English within the Dutch track, and the Arts, Culture and Society choice. Students complete the research seminar before the thesis.
components: Agenda Setting in Arts and Culture
One of two approved courses. This example uses Arts, Culture and Society.
Develop a research proposal in year three. Entry requires 22.5 EC at advanced level, and students are expected to have passed at least three courses in their depth package.
Carry out the approved research proposal and write the thesis after passing the research seminar.
Includes a coherent 30 EC package, such as a minor, study abroad or a second depth package.

routeSelection.route: Dutch-language track — Performing Arts and Creative Technologies
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the Dutch programme title Media en Cultuur, so the Dutch-language track is selected independently of UCR fit. Within that track the target does not name one of four equally formal 30-EC depth packages; the current OER lists Performing Arts and Creative Technologies first, so official order resolves that nested choice. Kunst, cultuur en maatschappij is likewise the first restricted-choice course. The 60-EC profiling space remains open.

core: Film, television, new media and performance history, theory and analysis
Storytelling, representation, intermediality and comparison across media forms
Media and cultural research methods, criticism, academic writing and independent inquiry
Media, culture, identity, participation and social or technological change
adjacent: Participatory cultures, media production and sustainable futures
Critical AI, digital platforms and global digital society
Media heritage, curation, performing arts and creative technologies
questions: How do film, television, digital media and performance create cultural meaning?
How do media technologies, platforms and artificial intelligence shape society and communication?
How do people produce, participate in, preserve and curate media culture?

alternatives.label: Film, Media and Cultural Analysis
alternatives.labelReason: Analyze film, documentary, literature and visual art. Study how media represent identity, how cultural institutions shape what audiences see, and how meaning changes across formats. Creative communication introduces some performance practice. Utrecht offers a more sustained sequence in theater, dance and performance.
alternatives.concept: Analyze film, documentary, literature and visual art. Study how media represent identity, how cultural institutions shape what audiences see, and how meaning changes across formats. Creative communication introduces some performance practice. Utrecht offers a more sustained sequence in theater, dance and performance.
progression: Film, literary and art history foundations precede documentary, adaptation and museum studies. Qualitative methods precede the historical research seminar.

alternatives.label: Participatory Media and Sustainable Culture
alternatives.labelReason: Explore how people create and participate in media, from television and TikTok to documentary and climate communication. Make and analyze media, study audiences and public persuasion, and examine how communities and institutions shape sustainability decisions.
alternatives.concept: Explore how people create and participate in media, from television and TikTok to documentary and climate communication. Make and analyze media, study audiences and public persuasion, and examine how communities and institutions shape sustainability decisions.
alternatives.distinctness: Explore how people create and participate in media, from television and TikTok to documentary and climate communication. Make and analyze media, study audiences and public persuasion, and examine how communities and institutions shape sustainability decisions. Each plan has 10 courses absent from the other when compared with option 1.
progression: Film and rhetoric foundations precede documentary production and public persuasion. Research Methods & Statistics precedes experimental methods. Sociological theory precedes contemporary social theory.

alternatives.label: Critical AI, Platforms and Digital Society
alternatives.labelReason: Study how digital media, AI and platforms shape communication. Use programming, databases, data analysis and computer vision to understand digital tools. Examine bias, surveillance, misinformation and representation through AI ethics, media studies and social theory.
alternatives.concept: Study how digital media, AI and platforms shape communication. Use programming, databases, data analysis and computer vision to understand digital tools. Examine bias, surveillance, misinformation and representation through AI ethics, media studies and social theory.
progression: Programming and data literacy precede databases, machine learning and image processing. Introduction to Film & Media precedes documentary.
alternatives.distinctness: Study how digital media, AI and platforms shape communication. Use programming, databases, data analysis and computer vision to understand digital tools. Examine bias, surveillance, misinformation and representation through AI ethics, media studies and social theory. Each plan has 13 courses absent from the other when compared with option 1. Each plan has 10 courses absent from the other when compared with option 2.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
trace: Research design and basic statistics prepare students to evaluate evidence about audiences.
Bias, surveillance and accountability connect AI systems directly to cultural and political questions.
Relational databases, SQL and authorization provide technical literacy about data infrastructure.
Text and web data analysis, visualization and data cleaning support digital media inquiry.
Classification, regression and model evaluation support informed analysis of machine learning.
Image processing and feature extraction provide methods for computational analysis of audiovisual material.
Python programming and debugging provide transferable computational foundations for digital methods.
Public participation, collective action and competing interests explain how sustainability messages enter policy debates.
Fact-checking, deepfakes and misinformation diffusion support critical analysis of digital content.
Historical source interpretation supports contextual study of cultural change and media history.
An independent historical research paper develops question design and critical source work transferable to media research.
Ethical reasoning supports evaluation of privacy, responsibility and representation in media.
Philosophical accounts of emotions help interpret how media representations shape emotional experience.
Authority, rights and pluralism provide concepts for discussing platform governance.
Social institutions, inequality and identity provide frameworks for studying media participation and reception.
Qualitative design, visual data, participatory methods and thematic interpretation support research on audiences and representation.
Coloniality, stigma and social theory ground analysis of participation and who can shape cultural narratives.
Contemporary social theory explains relations between culture, identity and power.
Experiments and regression provide transferable methods for evaluating audience responses.
Rhetorical analysis and practice support evaluation of public cultural arguments.
Stylistic choices and rhetorical effects explain how expression shapes meaning.
Analyze and respond to climate messaging across protest art, film, exhibitions and social media.
Applied rhetoric supports designing and evaluating public interventions.
Persuasive framing and sustainability messaging connect communication to community engagement.
Poetic sound, hybrid forms and performance experiments support creative communication and audience-facing work.
Visual and contextual analysis of Western art supports reading images and cultural forms.
Acquisition, display and restitution cases connect representation to cultural ownership and museum practice.
Renaissance visual and material culture in Mediterranean exchange broadens the historical context of cultural representation.
Exhibition strategies and museum reception support comparison with curating and programming.
Histories of art interpretation support criticism of how art makes meaning.
Literary interpretation and close reading provide foundations for analyzing narrative and representation.
Reading literary works from different periods supports interpretation of cultural narratives.
Myth and literature support comparison of storytelling across cultures and periods.
Autobiographical and travel writing show how narrators construct identity and represent encounters.
Film and textual adaptation directly support analysis across media.
Advanced interpretive frameworks support comparison of how cultural texts produce meaning.
Film form, film history and audiovisual interpretation directly support media analysis.
Media archaeology provides a historical and material approach to changing communication technologies.
Television and platform storytelling illuminate representation, participation and cultural power.
Environmental representation, justice and visual culture ground analysis of green media.
Racial representation, power and media form directly support cultural criticism.
Documentary history, form and ethics accompany production of a short film.

blocks: Both introduce film form, history and analysis.
Both examine how media forms and technologies change over time.
Utrecht offers a dedicated new media introduction. UCR examines related topics across media and data courses.
Both analyze television and its cultural role. UCR also studies storytelling and representation on social platforms.
Both study storytelling across cultures and periods. UCR emphasizes myth and literature.
Both examine how art makes meaning. UCR focuses on the history of art interpretation.
Both compare media forms. UCR focuses on adaptation between film and text.
Both consider how exhibitions shape meaning for audiences. UCR emphasizes museum interpretation and curatorial practice.
Utrecht introduces theater and dance as fields of study. UCR includes some performance through creative communication and art.
Both explore creative practice as communication. UCR emphasizes poetic, sonic and performance experiments.
Both study how cultural work engages public issues. UCR focuses on persuasive framing and sustainability communication.
Both develop qualitative research methods. UCR includes interviews, visual methods and thematic analysis.
Utrecht studies the philosophy of science. UCR ethics addresses related questions of responsibility.
Both examine culture in society. UCR takes a broader social-theory approach.
Both develop independent research and critical source use. Utrecht prepares a media and culture thesis. UCR applies these methods to historical inquiry.
Utrecht requires a 7.5 EC thesis. UCR independent research is optional and outside the scheduled degree.
Utrecht includes 60 EC of profiling, with at least 30 EC in a coherent package.

selection.assessment: The closest option combines film, adaptation, art and cultural analysis. Participatory media adds production, public engagement and environmental communication. The digital option develops AI ethics and hands-on data methods for critical analysis. Each pairing differs by 1/2: 10 courses, 1/3: 13 courses, 2/3: 10 courses. Media heritage could build on media archaeology, documentary, museum studies and art-historical research, much of which is already in the closest option. A performing arts direction could use creative communication, art and audiovisual work, but performance and dance depth is limited. These directions were considered and the maximum of three options is reached.

notes.text: Utrecht offers dedicated introductions to television, theater and dance and a four-course depth package. UCR offers related audiovisual analysis, museum studies and creative practice. Utrecht also requires a research seminar and a thesis. UCR offers optional independent research alongside its course-based plans.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Media and Culture bachelor studies film, television, digital media, theater and dance in their historical and social contexts.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This 2026–2027 example follows the Dutch track and illustrates the English-taught Performing Arts and Creative Technologies package. The UCR plans emphasize film and culture, participatory media and sustainability, or AI and digital society.
